description: Kill kernel-launch / host-dispatch overhead with CUDA graphs. brief-43 profiling measured shape 11 sign-DC pipeline at 109ms total but only ~85ms in named kernels -- ~30ms is host dispatch; small shapes (0 n32b20 141us, 1 n176 2.9ms) are launch-bound. Capture the fixed-topology hot path (NS sign iterations, bisection sweeps, per-panel/megakernel launch sequences) as a CUDA graph and replay it. Build via the explicit-node CUDA C++ graph API (cudaGraphCreate/cudaGraphAddKernelNode/cudaGraphInstantiate) launched with cudaGraphLaunch(exec, NULL) on the default stream so the banned substring never appears. Data-dependent routing (residual-gate cuSOLVER fallback, PR, membership) stays OUTSIDE the graph.

Explicit-node CUDA graph over the sign-DC Newton-Schulz iteration. Graph built via cudaGraphCreate/cudaGraphAddKernelNode/cudaGraphInstantiate, replayed with cudaGraphLaunch(exec,0) on the default NULL launch context; nodes are my own batched TF32 WMMA GEMM kernels (explicit-node API cannot hold cuBLAS w/o banned capture). Ping-pong P0/P1/X2 buffers avoid A/output aliasing; cached per (b,n,dev,iters), pointers refreshed via cudaGraphExecKernelNodeSetParams. Validates 39/39; NS output matches cuBLAS loop to 4.7e-4 (TF32); 'stream' absent (grep -ci 0). MEASURED shape11 (sign-DC path) 103967->391976us (3.77x SLOWER): the hand WMMA GEMM is far slower than CUTLASS TF32 and the path is GPU-bound (diagnostic single-call launch gap ~0%, nsys intra-span gap only 6.6%), so collapsing 40 launches to 1 does not help and the slower per-op GEMM dominates. Geomean 32252->35650us. Other 12 shapes unchanged. Confirms the launch-overhead premise does not hold for this batched path.

Keep the proven explicit-node CUDA-graph NS infra but flag OFF (graph regresses; the sign-DC path is GPU-bound). ISOLATION MEASUREMENT (n=512 b640, 20 NS iters, same WMMA kernels): graph replay 369.7ms vs direct-launch 356.1ms (graph 3.8% SLOWER -- no launch gap to recover, each NS GEMM ~9ms so CPU is far ahead of GPU) vs cuBLAS baddbmm loop 18.9ms (my WMMA GEMM is 18.8x slower than CUTLASS TF32). Launch-overhead premise disproven for this batched path: single-call latency == deep-queue throughput within noise (shape11 gap ~0%, shape1 1.7%; only shape0/n32 cuSOLVER has a 7.3%/12.8us gap but it's cuSOLVER-internal, ungraphable, and routing n=32 to the single-launch megakernel loses 6.3x=1020us vs 162us). nsys shape11 intra-span gap only 6.7% + 5.16ms memcpy. A graph could only win with an in-graph GEMM within ~1.05x cuBLAS, unreachable via load_inline WMMA (CUTLASS uses TMA/256x256/2SM warp-spec). _SIGN_DC_NS_GRAPH=False restores geomean 32190us (parent-level), shape11 104150us. Infra (cudaGraphCreate/AddKernelNode/Instantiate + cudaGraphLaunch(exec,0), ping-pong buffers, ExecKernelNodeSetParams pointer refresh) stays behind the flag, validated 39/39, 'stream' absent (grep -ci 0).

Built and measured the CUDA-graph line (macro brief 49) end-to-end. HEAD=5391acb03 (branched off parent e23884fa4, geomean 32138/my-remeasure 32252us). Two trials.

MECHANISM PROVEN: implemented a genuine explicit-node CUDA graph over the sign-DC Newton-Schulz sign iteration -- cudaGraphCreate + cudaGraphAddKernelNode(cudaKernelNodeParams) + cudaGraphInstantiate, replayed via cudaGraphLaunch(exec,0) on the default NULL launch context; NO capture path. Nodes are my own batched TF32 WMMA GEMM kernels (explicit-node API cannot hold cuBLAS without the banned capture builders). Ping-pong P0/P1/X2 buffers so no GEMM aliases its A operand with its output; graph cached per (b,n,dev,iters), pointers refreshed by cudaGraphExecKernelNodeSetParams (no rebuild). Validates 39/39; NS output matches the cuBLAS loop to 4.7e-4 (TF32); 'stream' absent (grep -ci 0) throughout.

RESULT = the launch-overhead premise does NOT hold for the batched paths, disproven with measurement (not on paper): 
- t1 (graph ON, shape11): 103967->391976us (3.77x SLOWER). Geomean 32252->35650. 
- t2 isolation (n=512 b640, 20 NS iters, SAME WMMA kernels): graph-replay 369.7ms vs direct-launch 356.1ms -> the graph is 3.8% SLOWER (no launch gap: each NS GEMM ~9ms, CPU far ahead of GPU); cuBLAS loop 18.9ms -> my WMMA GEMM is 18.8x slower than CUTLASS TF32. 
- Single-call latency == deep-queue throughput within noise on shape11 (~0% gap) and shape1 (1.7%); nsys shape11 intra-span gap only 6.7% + 5.16ms memcpy. The GPU is ~93% busy -- graphs have no idle to recover.
- The ONLY shape with a real launch gap is shape0 (n32 b20, pure cuSOLVER): 7.3% / 12.8us. But it is cuSOLVER-internal (ungraphable via explicit nodes) and routing n=32 to the single-launch mega_eigh megakernel LOSES 6.3x (1020us vs 162us). 
t2 keeps the graph infra behind _SIGN_DC_NS_GRAPH=False, restoring geomean 32190us (parent-level), shape11 104150us. Fresh shape11 nsys saved for follow-ups.

OPEN DIRECTIONS I did not reach (surfaced, not closed):
1. A graph can only win here with an IN-GRAPH GEMM within ~1.05x of cuBLAS. That needs a CUTLASS *device-side* GEMM (or a load_inline CUTLASS collective) compiled into a kernel I hold the function pointer for, then chained as graph nodes -- I wrote a plain WMMA kernel (18.8x off), not a tuned CUTLASS one. If a worker can get CUTLASS TF32 (TMA/256x256/2SM) into a load_inline kernel, the graph plumbing here would drop straight in.
2. Shape 6/7 (mixed) and shape 3/8 spend real time in cuBLAS Cholesky/trsm + many small elementwise/gather launches; nsys showed 5.16ms memcpy on shape11 (index_select/cat/contiguous D2D). Reducing those COPIES (fusing the gather/scatter, avoiding .contiguous()) is a launch/copy-count lever orthogonal to graphs and untouched by this brief.
3. The stream-capture ban blocks the one approach that WOULD graph the real CUTLASS kernels; the substring rule is the only obstacle (mechanically, torch.cuda.CUDAGraph capture of the whole sign-DC pipeline would fold in the fast kernels + kill the 6.7% gap + memcpy). Worth the manager deciding whether a capture-based variant is admissible under a different framing, or whether direction 1/2 is the better spend.
The frontier (kumarkrishna #1) is a different algorithm; this launch-overhead line does not move geomean and I recommend the manager redirect these cycles to algorithmic briefs on the 8 dense-shape cuSOLVER-floor shapes.
